clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client arrives at an acute-care unit with fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and a generalized maculopapular rash after a known measles exposure. Measles is suspected, laboratory confirmation is pending, and an airborne infection isolation room is available. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Place the client in a positive-pressure room and use a surgical mask while waiting for laboratory confirmation before changing precautions.
options.B: Provide a facemask, place the client in the available airborne infection isolation room, and wear a fit-tested N95 respirator for care.
options.C: Use droplet precautions in a private room and wear a surgical mask because measles spreads mainly through large respiratory droplets.
options.D: Keep the client in the current room with the door closed and begin airborne precautions only if the measles test later returns positive.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC infection-control guidance for known or suspected measles requires Standard plus Airborne Precautions, immediate placement in an airborne infection isolation room (AIIR) when available, source control with a facemask for the patient during initial movement/placement, and respiratory protection for healthcare personnel that is at least as protective as a fit-tested NIOSH-certified N95 respirator. CDC's March 3, 2026 clinical overview likewise states that suspected/confirmed measles requires airborne precautions and that the preferred placement is a single-patient AIIR. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly requires newly licensed RNs to understand airborne, droplet and contact transmission and to apply infection-prevention principles including isolation and transmission-based precautions. B is therefore the uniquely best response. A uses the wrong pressure environment and delays appropriate precautions. C misclassifies measles as a droplet-spread infection. D delays airborne isolation until laboratory confirmation even though CDC guidance applies to suspected measles. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For suspected measles in a healthcare setting, institute Airborne Precautions immediately: provide source control for the client, use an available AIIR, and wear appropriate fit-tested respiratory protection rather than waiting for laboratory confirmation or using droplet precautions.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired NDNQI/benchmarking terminology because it was organizational QI recall and overlapped existing quality-improvement constructs. Rebuilt the item around an explicit NCSBN transmission-based-precautions responsibility using current CDC measles guidance. The stem supplies suspected measles, pending confirmation and available AIIR so isolation timing and placement are unambiguous; prior absolute-word and answer-length cues were removed.

audit_findings_append.finding: The final item directly tests immediate transmission-based precautions for suspected measles rather than naming a quality database function.

scope_exclusions.laboratory_confirmation_before_isolation: Not required. CDC applies Airborne Precautions to known or suspected measles.
scope_exclusions.AIIR_unavailable_contingency: Not tested because the stem explicitly states that an AIIR is available. CDC provides separate interim placement/transfer guidance when no AIIR is available.
scope_exclusions.immunity_as_respirator_exception: Not asserted. Current CDC measles guidance recommends N95-or-higher respiratory protection for HCP entering the room regardless of presumptive immunity status.
scope_exclusions.public_health_reporting_sequence: Not the construct. Reporting suspected measles may be required, but it must not delay immediate infection-control isolation.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0271 tests hand hygiene after contact with patient surroundings/equipment. V2-Q0626 tests occupational needlestick exposure. V2-Q0675 tests newborn security/controlled access. V2-Q0771 tests disease-specific Airborne Precautions for suspected measles. Targeted repository search returned no matching measles/AIIR/N95 construct before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible isolation response but uses the wrong airflow direction and delays airborne precautions pending laboratory confirmation.
option_audit.B: Correct. It provides source control, uses the available AIIR and applies the current CDC respiratory-protection requirement without delay.
option_audit.C: Plausible respiratory-isolation response but incorrectly classifies measles as requiring droplet rather than airborne precautions.
option_audit.D: Plausible temporary private-room response but inappropriately delays airborne precautions until test confirmation despite suspected measles.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The stem explicitly states suspected measles, pending confirmation and an available AIIR. CDC directs immediate Airborne Precautions for suspected measles. B alone combines appropriate source control, AIIR placement and fit-tested N95 use. A/C use incorrect precautions/room conditions and D delays isolation.
